_comment: What this skill says out loud, declared so it can be recorded ahead of time.
Lesson prompts are NOT listed here — generate-voice.mjs collects those from
this skill's lessons.json, so authoring a lesson never means editing this file.
What belongs here is speech that lives in the skill's code: numbers, and the
fixed or templated lines an activity says. Anything missing is not broken, only
slower: an unrecorded phrase falls back to server TTS and then to the browser.
_numberRangeComment: FroggySkip speaks every pad it lands on. `count-by-10s-up-to-100` hops by 10 up to six times, so it says 60 — the range was 0-50 and that last hop fell through to the browser's voice. Derived from the numberline lessons' steps and hop ranges; widen this if either grows.
_templateComment: A template is expanded into one recorded line per value.
A bare string uses `subjects` — the countable objects TouchOrbit names.
The object form carries its own `values`, which is how a prompt containing a
number gets recorded: the ten-frame says 'Make 19. Fill one frame with 10,
then add more.' and that is nine fixed sentences, not one dynamic one.
Only worth it where the range is small and matches the lesson. Base10's
prompts interpolate three values over hundreds of targets — not a list, and
they stay on live TTS. Ranges here must track lessons.json: ten-frame fill
templates: Touch each {value}. Count as you go!
Touch every {value}. Do not miss any!

templates.text: Make {value} dots. Fill the top row first.
You have {value}. How many more to make 10?
Make {value}. Fill one frame with 10, then add more.

_groupsComment: Reactions to an answer, picked at random so a child does not hear the same
clip forty times in a session — which is how praise stops meaning anything.
`voices` rotates across the phrases, so the variants differ in who is speaking
as well as in wording. Names are Gemini's prebuilt voices; Charon and Fenrir
are deliberately left out as too grave for a five-year-old being congratulated.
The `incorrect` lines never say wrong, bad or no. A child at this age reads a
flat 'incorrect' as a verdict on themselves, and the round already lets them
try again — the voice's job is to keep them in it, not to grade them.
_phrasesComment: Lines an activity says in passing — not the question itself.
Base10 says these when ten ones become a ten, mid-drag. They are commentary
on what just happened, which is why they are not prompts.
_promptsComment: What an activity says as the question — the thing being asked.
Kept apart from `phrases` so the folder on disk says what a clip is: every
file in audio/prompts is a question, every file in audio/phrases is an aside.
Moving a line between these lists moves its recording; it is not re-recorded.
prompts: Look fast! How many did you see?
How many dots did you see?
Count both groups. Do they have the same?
Count both groups. Which one has more?
Add more blocks to make the number.
